subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support a Slack user-identity mode that receives user-authorized `message.im` events and replies through the configured user token as that Slack user?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent behavior changes Slack identity, authorization, token selection, and operator expectations, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary alone.

options.title: Support explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Add a clearly named opt-in mode with live Slack proof, docs, and tests for authorizing-user routing and reply-token selection while keeping bot-token behavior as the default.

options.title: Keep bot identity only
options.body: Document that Slack user tokens are for read/look-up support and that natural no-app-badge user impersonation is not an OpenClaw-supported Slack mode.

options.title: Defer pending live proof
options.body: Ask for a live Slack Socket Mode transcript showing user-level envelopes reaching OpenClaw before deciding whether the mode should exist.

recommendation.title: Support explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Add a clearly named opt-in mode with live Slack proof, docs, and tests for authorizing-user routing and reply-token selection while keeping bot-token behavior as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current signal on Slack token identity, maintainer follow-through, and the surrounding monitor/provider behavior.
